functionalReqs: Offline delivery when the user reconnects
hints: HTTP polling, long polling or WebSockets: which suits server-to-client pushes at this scale?
Chat servers hold WebSocket connections; how does server A find which server user B is connected to?

Use a session/presence service (user → chat server) in Redis, a message store partitioned by chat ID (Cassandra or HBase), per-chat sequence numbers for ordering, an inbox queue for offline users, push notifications as fallback, and group fan-out via a message queue.
nonFunctionalReqs: Real-time delivery (under 300 ms when both are online)
No message loss; order preserved within a chat
problemStatement:
Design a **chat app** like WhatsApp with one-to-one and group messaging, online presence, and sent/delivered/read receipts.

Messages must arrive in order, survive the recipient being offline, and be delivered with low latency.

referenceLinks.title: How Discord stores trillions of messages

scaleHints.storage: ~100 bytes per message; messages kept until delivered (or for history)
